keywords.help: Title of the case being considered.
Number of processors for domain partition. Value 0 corresponds to a scalar computation.
If this keyword is equal to YES, a call to subroutine CHECKMESH will look for errors in the mesh, superimposed points, etc.
Maximal number of boundaries in the mesh. Used for dimensioning arrays. Can be increased if needed.

Name of the file containing the types of boundary conditions. This file is filled automatically by the mesh generator through colours that are assigned to the boundary nodes.
Binary-coded data file containing the boundary conditions data varying in time and space.

Name of the FORTRAN file or directory to be submitted, including specific subroutines of the model.
Name of the possible file containing the bathymetric data. Where this keyword is used, these bathymetric data shall be used in the computation.
Number of smoothings on bottom topography. Each smoothing is mass conservative. To be used when interpolation of bathymetry on the mesh gives very rough results.

Formatted data file available to the user.
Formatted data file available to the user.
Data file in binary mode available to the user.

Data file in binary mode available to the user.

Binary-coded result file for validation. This option is primarily used for the validation documents. This reference file is then considered as a reference which the computation is going to be compared with. The comparison is done by the subroutine BIEF_VALIDA, which can be modified so as to include, for example, a comparison with an exact solution. If present in the steering file, triggers the validation step during the computation since release 9.0 without boolean keyword VALIDATION.

Format of the REFERENCE FILE. Possible choices are: SERAFIN : classical single precision format in TELEMAC, SERAFIND: classical double precision format in TELEMAC, MED : MED double precision format based on HDF5.
Name of the file containing points coordinates and periods of time where time series are extracted in the TIME SERIES FILE (2D or 3D).
Name of the file into which the 3D results of the computation are written with a periodicity given by the keyword GRAPHIC PRINTOUT PERIOD.

Format of the 2D RESULT FILE. Possible choices are: SERAFIN : classical single precision format in TELEMAC, SERAFIND: classical double precision format in TELEMAC, MED : MED double precision format based on HDF5.
Gives the coordinates of the result file in longitude-latitude if the geometry file is also given in longitude-latitude.

You can ask for: U : velocity along x (m/s), V : velocity along y (m/s), W : velocity along z (m/s), Z : elevation z (m), TAi: concentration of tracer i, i is the tracer number, TA*: concentration of every tracer, TA1*: concentration of tracers from 10 to 19, NUX: viscosity for velocities along x (m^2/s), NUY: viscosity for velocities along y (m^2/s), NUZ: viscosity for velocities along z (m^2/s), NAXi: viscosity for tracer i along x (m^2/s), NAYi: viscosity for tracer i along y (m^2/s), NAZi: viscosity for tracer i along z (m^2/s), NAX*: viscosity for every tracer along x (m^2/s), NAY*: viscosity for every tracer along y (m^2/s), NAZ*: viscosity for every tracer along z (m^2/s), RI : Richardson number for mixing length model, K : turbulent kinetic energy for k-epsilon model (J/kg), EPS: dissipation of turbulent kinetic energy (W/kg), DP : dynamic pressure (multiplied by DT/RHO), PH : hydrostatic pressure (Pa), RHO: relative density, P1 : private variable 1, P2 : private variable 2, P3 : private variable 3, P4 : private variable 4, US : Stokes velocity along x axis (m/s), VS : Stokes velocity along y axis (m/s), WS : Stokes velocity along z axis (m/s), CSO2: oxygen saturation concentration (mgO2/l), O2SAT: percentage of oxygen saturation (%).

choices.V: depth averaged velocity along y axis (m/s)

Format of the 2D TIME SERIES FILE. Possible choices are: SERAFIN : classical single precision format in TELEMAC, SERAFIND: classical double precision format in TELEMAC, MED : MED double precision format based on HDF5.
Name of the file into which 3D time series are written at the points defined in the TIME SERIES COORDINATES FILE.

Result printout on hard copy. When NO is selected, the listing only includes the heading and the phrase 'NORMAL END OF PROGRAM'. In addition, the options MASS-BALANCE and VALIDATION are inhibited. Not recommended for use.

Determines whether a check of the mass-balance over the domain is done or not. This procedures computes the following at each time step: the domain inflows and outflows, the overall flow across all the boundaries, the relative error in the mass for that time step. The relative error in the mass over the whole computation can be found at the end of the listing.

keywords.keyword: INFORMATION ABOUT MASS-BALANCE FOR EACH LISTING PRINTOUT
keywords.help: Gives the information about mass-balance at every LISTING PRINTOUT PERIOD.
Determines, in number of time steps, the printout period of the VARIABLES TO BE PRINTED. The results are systematically printed out on the listing file.

keywords.keyword: NUMBER OF FIRST TIME STEP FOR LISTING PRINTOUTS
keywords.help: Determines the number of time steps after which the results are first written into the listing.
Sections input file, partitioned.
Sections output file, written by the master.
Printing the cumulated flowrates through control sections.
Flowrates through control sections, computation compatible with the weak formulation of no-flux boundary condition.

Name of a file containing the results of an earlier computation which was made on the same mesh. One recorded time step will provide the initial conditions for the new computation. If present in the steering file, a continuation is done from the result of a previous computation defined by this keyword without boolean keyword COMPUTATION CONTINUED since release 9.0. In that case, all the data from the steering file may be defined once again, which provides an opportunity to change, for example, the time step, the turbulence model, the friction, to add or remove a tracer... It is also possible to define new boundary conditions (in the subroutine BORD3D or values defined in the steering file). In case of a perfect continued computation, the PREVIOUS COMPUTATION FILE has to be the RESTART FILE of the last computation. This last file is then an output file of the last computation. The PREVIOUS COMPUTATION FILE FORMAT and the RESTART FILE FORMAT have to be set with 'SERAFIND' or 'MED'.

Format of the PREVIOUS COMPUTATION FILE. Possible choices are: SERAFIN : classical single precision format in TELEMAC, SERAFIND: classical double precision format in TELEMAC, MED : MED double precision format based on HDF5.
In case of continuation of computation, record number to start from in the PREVIOUS COMPUTATION FILE. -1 means that the last record is taken.
Initial time set to zero in case of restart.

Name of the file into which the last computation results shall be written in order to get a perfect continued computation unlike using the 3D RESULT FILE. It is then an output file for the current computation, which will be used as an input file when a continued computation is expected to be perfect (the keyword PREVIOUS COMPUTATION FILE is then used). The RESTART FILE FORMAT and the PREVIOUS COMPUTATION FILE FORMAT have to be set with 'SERAFIND' or 'MED'. If present in the steering file, triggers the writing of this restart file since release 9.0 without boolean keyword RESTART MODE.

Format of the RESTART FILE. Possible choices are: SERAFIN : classical single precision format in TELEMAC, SERAFIND: classical double precision format in TELEMAC, MED : MED double precision format based on HDF5. Only double precision formats ensure a perfect restart.

Determines, in number of time steps, the printout period for the variables to be saved for a perfect restart in the RESTART FILE. Default = 0 means the RESTART FILE is only written at the last time step or at the RECORD NUMBER IN RESTART FILE.

Determines the number of time step when printing the variables to be saved for a perfect restart in the RESTART FILE. Default = -1 means the RESTART FILE is only written at the last time step and/or periodically at the period RESTART FILE PRINTOUT PERIOD.

keywords.keyword: USE MAXIMUM VALUES FROM PREVIOUS COMPUTATION FILE
keywords.help: If YES, computes maximum values for variables MAXZ, TMXZ from PREVIOUS COMPUTATION FILE and current computation. If NO, the variables are only computed from current computation.

Name of the file to be used in case of 2D continuation. It contains results of an earlier computation (a 2D computation or a 2D result file). One recorded time step will provide the initial conditions for the new computation. If present in the steering file, a 2D continuation is done from the result of a previous 2D computation or a 2D result file, defined by this keyword without boolean keyword 2D CONTINUATION since release 9.0.

Format of the FILE FOR 2D CONTINUATION. Possible choices are: SERAFIN : classical single precision format in TELEMAC, SERAFIND: classical double precision format in TELEMAC, MED : MED double precision format based on HDF5.
If 1, additional writings will be printed in the listing, in particular the calls of subroutines.
Specifies the time step in seconds.
Specifies the number of time steps performed when running the code.

Sets the duration of the simulation in seconds. May be used instead of the parameter NUMBER OF TIME STEPS. The nearest integer to (duration/time step) is taken. If NUMBER OF TIME STEPS is also given, the greater value is taken.

Enables to set the date of the time origin of the model when taking into account of the tide (tide generator force and/or the tidal boundary conditions). Also used with drogues, heat exchange with atmosphere, chaining with DELWAQ.

Enables to set the time of the time origin of the model when taking into account of the tide (tide generator force and/or the tidal boundary conditions). Also used with drogues, heat exchange with atmosphere, chaining with DELWAQ.
Initial time of the computation (in seconds).

Selection of spherical coordinates to perform the computation (for large computation domains). Warning: this option is closely related to the mesh that should have been entered onto a nautical chart drawn as per Mercator projection The LATITUDE OF ORIGIN POINT, which corresponds to ordinate y = 0 in the mesh, must moreover be given.

Specifies the type of spatial projection used (for example when using spherical coordinates). Possible choices are: 1: Cartesian, not georeferenced, 2: Mercator, 3: latitude/longitude (in degrees). Option 2 or 3 mandatory for spherical coordinates. Option 3: latitude and longitude in degrees! When using option 3, the coordinates are automatically treated by TELEMAC-3D using Mercator projection. Old default value = 2 until release 8.5.
Gives the value of the latitude of the origin point of the mesh (for the Mercator projection, see the keyword GEOGRAPHIC SYSTEM). Also used for heat exchange with atmosphere.
Gives the value of the longitude of the origin point of the mesh (for the Mercator projection, see the keyword GEOGRAPHIC SYSTEM). Also used for tide generating force, heat exchange with atmosphere.
Angle of North, counted counter-clockwise, with Oy. Read but not used.
Gives the number of planes from bottom to free surface. Must be at least 2.

Specifies the distribution of vertical planes of the mesh. Possible choices are: 0: user defined (then subroutine CALCOT to be implemented), 1: sigma, 2: zstar, 3: horizontal fixed planes, 4: sigma with zooming factor, 5: adaptive mesh. This keyword must comply with what is done in CONDIM subroutine.

Mesh transformation coefficients (which must be larger than 0). The first determines the vertical mesh stretching near the bottom, the second the vertical stretching near the free surface. Only used with MESH TRANSFORMATION = 4.
Minimum volume of 3D elements in m^3.

keywords.keyword: MINIMUM DISTANCE BETWEEN PLANES CLOSE TO THE BOTTOM
keywords.help: Minimum distance between planes close to the bottom. Only for planes of type TRANSF_PLANE%I(...) = 3.

keywords.keyword: MINIMUM DISTANCE BETWEEN PLANES CLOSE TO THE FREE SURFACE
keywords.help: Minimum distance between planes close to the free surface. Only for planes of type TRANSF_PLANE%I(...) = 3.
Minimum height below which 3D elements are treated as crushed. This is not done for the free surface plane.
Specifies the number of tracer used by the adaptive mesh algorithm (MESH TRANSFORMATION = 5).

keywords.keyword: NUMBER OF SUB ITERATIONS FOR NON LINEARITIES
keywords.help: Used for updating, within one time step, the advection and propagation fields. Upon the first sub-iteration, these fields are given by C and the velocity field in the previous time step. At subsequent iterations, the results of the previous sub-iteration is used to update the advection and propagation field. The non-linearities can be taken into account through this technique.
Not used so far.
Takes into account the advection terms or not. If YES, some advection terms can still be ignored with the keywords SCHEME FOR ADVECTION OF...

keywords.keyword: TREATMENT OF FLUXES AT THE BOUNDARIES
keywords.help: Used so far only with the SUPG, PSI and N schemes (one integer per open boundary). Possible choices are: 1: priority to prescribed values, 2: priority to fluxes. With option 2, Dirichlet prescribed values are not obeyed, but the fluxes are correct.

Specifies the type of upwinding used. Possible choices are: 0: no upwinding, 1: classical SUPG, 2: modified SUPG. The same choice is applied to U, V and W, but also to tracer(s), k and epsilon if needed.

keywords.keyword: MAXIMUM NUMBER OF ITERATIONS FOR ADVECTION SCHEMES
keywords.help: Limits the number of solver iterations for the advection schemes, only for schemes 13 and 14. Old default value = 10 until release 8.1.

keywords.keyword: NUMBER OF SUB-STEPS OF DISTRIBUTIVE SCHEMES
keywords.help: Only for implicit scheme with predictor-corrector (4 or 5). This keyword allows to subdivide the time step given by the user in the STEERING FILE, into several sub-steps. Again, it produces an effect on the precision of the scheme and it is convenient to set this keyword in order to have Courant numbers not too large (around 1).

keywords.keyword: NUMBER OF CORRECTIONS OF DISTRIBUTIVE SCHEMES
keywords.help: For predictor-corrector options with advection scheme of type 3, 4, 5, LIPS or not). Number of iterations for every time step (or sub-time step) to converge to the solution. It is useful for unsteady cases. For quasi-steady flows, this keyword does not have a large impact on the solution, so it can be set to 0. On the other hand, for unsteady flows, it is suggested to set this keyword to 2 (at least), which is a good compromise between accuracy and computational time. Indeed, increasing the number of corrections the scheme is more accurate but the CPU time rapidly increases.

Mass-lumping of the mass-matrix in the diffusion step. If diffusion is explicit (IMPLICITATION FOR DIFFUSION < 0.001) or if the advection scheme is of type 3, 4, 5, 13 or 14, it is automatically set to 1. in DIFF3D.
Specifies the use of the non-hydrostatic code version or not.
If YES, fill in the subroutine MASKOB.
Sets the value of the acceleration due to gravity in m/s^2.
Average water density in the domain, see subroutine DRSURR.

Selects the type of formulation used for the bottom friction. The possible laws are as follows (refer to the Principle note): 0: no friction against bottom, 1: Haaland's formula, 2: Chezy's formula, 3: Strickler's formula, 4: Manning's formula, 5: Nikuradse's formula. Old default value = 2 (Chezy) until version V7P3 and 0 (no friction) in V8P0.
Friction coefficient on the bottom, if constant. Old default value = 60. until version V8P0.

keywords.keyword: LAW OF FRICTION ON LATERAL BOUNDARIES
keywords.help: Selects the type of formulation used for the friction on lateral boundaries. The possible laws are as follows (refer to the Principle note): 0: no friction, or AUBOR given by the BOUNDARY CONDITION FILE, 5: Nikuradse's formula.

choices.1: COEFFICIENT TAKEN IN BOUNDARY CONDITIONS FILE

keywords.keyword: FRICTION COEFFICIENT FOR LATERAL SOLID BOUNDARIES
keywords.help: Friction coefficient on the lateral boundaries, if constant. Old default value = 60. until version V8P0.
The Coriolis force is taken into account or ignored.

Sets the value of the Coriolis force coefficient, in cartesian coordinates. This coefficient, denoted FCOR in the code, should be equal to 2 omega sin(l) where omega denotes the earth angular speed of rotation and l the latitude. omega = 7.29 10-5 rad/s. The Coriolis force components are then: FU = FCOR x V, FV = -FCOR x U. When using the spherical coordinates, the Coriolis coefficient is automatically computed.
Determines whether the wind effects are to be taken into account or not.

Gives the option for managing the wind: 1: constant in time and space, given by the keywords WIND VELOCITY ALONG X and WIND VELOCITY ALONG Y, 2: variable in time and constant in space, given by formatted file, 3: variable in time and space, given by formatted file or by a binary file.

choices.2: variable in time given by formatted file
choices.3: variable in time and space given by formatted file

keywords.help: Wind velocity, component along x axis (m/s), if constant.
Wind velocity, component along y axis (m/s), if constant.
Sets the value of the wind driving coefficient. See the User Manual for the value to give.

keywords.keyword: COEFFICIENT OF WIND INFLUENCE VARYING WITH WIND SPEED
keywords.help: If YES, the value of the wind driving coefficient is computed with respect to the wind velocity. The value of COEFFICIENT OF WIND INFLUENCE is overwritten. Old default value = NO until V8P1.
Wind is not taken into account for depths smaller than this value.
Sets whether the influence of an atmosphere pressure field is taken into account or not.
Gives the value of atmospheric pressure when it is constant in time and space. In Pa.
Enables to add or remove water at the free surface. See the keyword RAIN OR EVAPORATION IN MM PER DAY.

keywords.keyword: RAIN OR EVAPORATION IN MM PER DAY
keywords.help: Specifies the amount of water to add or remove at the free surface.
ASCII data file containing the atmospheric data varying in time.
Binary-coded data file containing the atmospheric data varying in time and space on the mesh.

Format of the BINARY ATMOSPHERIC DATA FILE. Possible choices are: SERAFIN : classical single precision format in TELEMAC, SERAFIND: classical double precision format in TELEMAC, MED : MED double precision format based on HDF5.

keywords.keyword: FREE FORMAT FOR ATMOSPHERIC DATA FILE
keywords.help: Indicates if the atmospheric data file (ASCII or binary) has to follow the format expected by the METEO_TELEMAC module or if it can be handled outside this module. If a special treatment has to be implemented for this file, e.g. with option OPTION FOR WIND = 3, set to YES.
Gives the value of air temperature when it is constant in time and space. In degC.
Gives the value of cloud cover when it is constant in time and space. In octas for WAQTEL or tenths for KHIONE.
Gives the value of solar radiation when it is constant in time and space. In W/m^2.
Gives the value of relative humidity when it is constant in time and space. In %.
Gives the unit of (atmospheric) pressure. Possible choices: Pa (SI), hPa.
Name of the file containing time-dependent information on sources.
Global numbers of nodes in the 2D mesh that correspond to source point locations.
Defines how the sources are computed: 1: Source term multiplied by a finite element basis, 2: Source term multiplied by a Dirac function (recommended with high numbers of sources).
Floats giving the abscissae of potential sources of flow rates (in meters). The source will be located at the nearest node in the mesh.
Floats giving the ordinates of potential sources of flow rates (in meters). The source will be located at the nearest node in the mesh.

Sets the height of the sources. The source will be located at the nearest plane in the mesh. The use of a fixed plane is then recommended to avoid the change of the nearest plane in case of variation of local water height.
Specifies the discharge for every source. A positive discharge means that fluid is added.

keywords.keyword: VELOCITIES OF THE SOURCES ALONG X
keywords.help: Specifies the compoment along x of the velocities of the sources. If nothing is specified, the sources diffuse without any velocity in every direction (cf. validation case source).

keywords.keyword: VELOCITIES OF THE SOURCES ALONG Y
keywords.help: Specifies the compoment along y of the velocities of the sources. If nothing is specified, the sources diffuse without any velocity in every direction (cf. validation case source).

keywords.keyword: VELOCITIES OF THE SOURCES ALONG Z
keywords.help: Specifies the compoment along z of the velocities of the sources. If nothing is specified, the sources diffuse without any velocity in every direction (cf. validation case source).
Wave driven currents are taken into account, see subroutine TRISOU.
Record number to be read by TELEMAC-3D in the wave driven currents file.
Values of the elevations prescribed at open boundaries.
Values of the flowrates prescribed at open boundaries.
Values of the magnitudes of velocity prescribed at open boundaries.
File containing the variations in time of boundary conditions.

Specifies the type of horizontal profile of velocities (one integer per open boundary). Possible choices are: 1: constant normal profile, 2: u and v given in the BOUNDARY CONDITION FILE, 3: normal velocity given in UBOR in the BOUNDARY CONDITION FILE, 4: normal velocity in sqrth, 5: like 4 but virtual depth based on the lowest elevation of the boundary.

choices.2: ubor and vbor given in the conlim file
choices.3: normal velocity given in ubor in the conlim file
choices.5: like 4 with virtual depth, see help

keywords.help: Specifies the type of vertical profile of velocity (one integer per open boundary). Possible choices are: 0: defined by user, 1: constant, 2: logarithmic.
Specifies if a discharge-elevation curve must be used for a given boundary (one value per open boundary): 0: no, 1: Z(Q), 2: Q(Z). Not yet implemented.
Name of the file containing stage-discharge curves.

Relaxation coefficient used to interpolate free surface elevation with respect to flowrate from the stage-discharge curve (for STAGE-DISCHARGE CURVES = 1). If set to 1., the elevation is instantaneously prescribed corresponding to the stage-discharge curve, but this may lead to instabilities. Setting a value between 0. and 1., a delay is introduced to prescribe this stage-discharge curve, that is a compromise between the goal of the stage-discharge curve and possible instabilities. Read the TELEMAC-3D user manual for more details.
One integer per liquid boundary is given. Possible choices are: 1: classical boundary conditions, 2: Thompson method based on characteristics.
Defines the turbulence regime for the bottom in the case of a k-epsilon or mixing-length model: 1: smooth, 2: rough, 3: rough also (for compatibility with old versions).

keywords.keyword: TURBULENCE REGIME FOR LATERAL SOLID BOUNDARIES
keywords.help: Defines the turbulence regime for the lateral boundaries: 1: smooth, 2: rough.

Specifies the type of boundary conditions on the bottom layer. Possible choices are: 1: Neumann conditions on velocity on bottom, 2: velocities will be set to 0. Should be linked to a refined mesh near the bottom.

choices.1: LOG LAW FOR VELOCITIES ON BOTTOM
choices.2: NO SLIP FOR VELOCITIES ON BOTTOM

keywords.keyword: VELOCITY PROJECTED ON SOLID LATERAL BOUNDARIES
keywords.help: Will ensure U.n = 0 on solid lateral boundaries by a projection at the end of time loop.
Will ensure U.n = 0 on bottom by a projection at the end of time loop.

keywords.keyword: OPEN BOUNDARY CONDITIONS ON THE BED
keywords.help: Defines if there are open boundary conditions on the bed.
Sets the value for flow rate on flow rate-imposed bed boundaries.
One integer per liquid boundary is given. Possible choices are: 0: Not a soft boundary , 1: Method 1. Proportional to the speed, 2: Method 2. Proportional to the square of speed.

choices.2: Method 2. Proportional to the square of speed

keywords.help: Values of the coefficients for each soft boundary.

Makes it possible to define the initial conditions of the water depth. The possible values are as follows: ZERO ELEVATION: Initializes the free surface elevation to 0. The initial water depths are then found by computing the difference between the free surface and the bottom, CONSTANT ELEVATION: Initializes the water elevation to the value given by the keyword INITIAL ELEVATION. The initial water depths are computed as in the previous case, ZERO DEPTH: Initializes the water depths to 0. CONSTANT DEPTH: Initializes the water depths to the value given by the keyword INITIAL DEPTH, TPXO SATELITE ALTIMETRY: The initial conditions on the free surface and velocities are established from the satellite program data given by the harmonic constants database coming from OSU (e.g. TPXO) and stored in the BINARY DATABASE 1/2 FOR TIDE, SPECIAL or PARTICULAR: The initial conditions with the water depth should be stated in the USER_CONDI3D_H subroutine.
Value to be used with the option: INITIAL CONDITIONS : 'CONSTANT ELEVATION'.
Value to be used along with the option: INITIAL CONDITIONS : 'CONSTANT DEPTH'.
Defines the method to store matrices. The possible choices are: 1: classical EBE, 3: edge-based storage.

TELEMAC-3D offers the possibility to perform mass-lumping on H. This gathers all or part (given the value of the coefficient) of the AM1(H) matrices on their diagonal. This technique can speed-up the code a lot and also render it more stable. Yet, the solutions are smoothened. This parameter sets the mass-lumping amount done for H.
Allows to filter hydrostatic inconsistencies.
Specifies the type of elements used in the computation. The possible choices are: PRISM: superimposed meshes of triangles, TETRAHEDRON: the same but prisms are split into tetrahedrons.

Choice of the solver for the propagation equation. Possible choices are: 1: conjugate gradient, 2: conjugate residual, 3: conjugate gradient on a normal equation, 4: minimum error, 5: squared conjugate gradient, 6: CGSTAB, 7: GMRES, 8: direct solver. Old default value = 1 (conjugate gradient) until version V8P0.

choices.3: conjugate gradient on a normal equation

keywords.help: Sets the accuracy needed for the computation of the propagation step. Old default value = 1.E-6 until version V8P0.

keywords.keyword: MAXIMUM NUMBER OF ITERATIONS FOR PROPAGATION
keywords.help: Since the algorithms used for solving the propagation step are iterative, the allowed number of iterations should be limited. NOTE: a maximum number of 40 iterations per time step seems to be reasonable.

Choice of the preconditioning in the propagation step linear system that the convergence is speeded up when it is being solved. Possible choices are: 0: no preconditioning, 2: diagonal, 3: diagonal with the condensed matrix, 5: diagonal with absolute values, 7: Crout, 11: Gauss-Seidel EBE, 13: matrix defined by the user, 14: diagonal and Crout, 17: direct solver on the vertical, 21: diagonal condensed and Crout, 34: diagonal and direct solver on the vertical. Some operations (either 2 or 3 diagonal preconditioning) can be performed concurrently with the others. Only prime numbers are therefore kept to denote the preconditioning operations. When several of them are to be performed concurrently, the product of relevant options shall be done.

choices.34: diagonal and direct solver on the vertical

keywords.help: Dimension of Krylov space for the GMRES method (7). Old default value = 3 until version V8P0.

Initial guess for the solver in the propagation step. Makes it possible to modify the initial value of delta h, upon each iteration in the propagation step, by using the ultimate values this variable had in the earlier time steps. Thus, the convergence can be speeded up when the system is being solved. 3 options are available: 0: delta h = 0, 1: delta h = delta h_n (ultimate delta h value in the next previous time step), 2: delta h = 2 delta h_n - delta h_n-1 (extrapolation). If option 2 with the non-hydrostatic version, INITIAL GUESS FOR DEPTH is automatically set to 1.

Provided for linearizing the propagation step, e.g. when performing test-cases for which an analytical solution in the linearized case is available. Thus, the value of MEAN DEPTH FOR LINEARIZATION has to be given.
Sets the water depth about which the linearization is done when the LINEARIZED PROPAGATION option is selected.
The conservative scheme (5) is now mandatory.

Sets the advection scheme for the velocities. Possible choices are: 0: no convection, 1: characteristics, 2: explicit + SUPG, 3: explicit Leo Postma, 4: explicit + MURD scheme N, 5: explicit + MURD scheme PSI, 13: Leo Postma for tidal flats, 14: N-scheme for tidal flats. Default values for SCHEME FOR ADVECTION OF VELOCITIES = 5 + SCHEME OPTION FOR ADVECTION OF VELOCITIES = 4 give LIPS scheme. Old default value = 1 (characteristics) until version V8P0.
Values between 0 and 1 may suppress spurious oscillations.
Will speed-up distributive and finite volumes advection schemes in case of tidal flats or generalised sigma transformation.
Sets the amount of mass-lumping that is performed on the velocity. Read but not used.

keywords.keyword: SCHEME OPTION FOR ADVECTION OF VELOCITIES
keywords.help: If present replaces and has priority over: OPTION FOR CHARACTERISTICS and SUPG OPTION. If N or PSI scheme: 1: explicit, 2: predictor-corrector, 3: predictor-corrector second-order in time, 4: implicit (compatible with tidal flats). If no tidal flats, option 2 is faster. Old default value = 1 (explicit) until version V8P0.

Possible choices are: 1: strong form, 2: weak form. If SCHEME FOR ADVECTION OF... = 1 and also the corresponding keyword SCHEME OPTION FOR ADVECTION OF... = 2, OPTION FOR CHARACTERISTICS is automatically set to 2.

keywords.keyword: NUMBER OF GAUSS POINTS FOR WEAK CHARACTERISTICS
keywords.help: See release notes v6.3. Number of Gauss points used to compute the weak characteristics. 6 (points) is the only choice for TELEMAC-3D.
Sets the amount of mass-lumping that is applied to the mass matrix when using weak characteristics.
Monitors the choice of the diffusion scheme for velocities. Possible choices are: 0: no diffusion, 1: implicit.

Choice of the solver for the diffusion of velocities U and V. Possible choices are: 1: conjugate gradient, 2: conjugate residual, 3: conjugate gradient on a normal equation, 4: minimum error, 5: squared conjugate gradient, 6: CGSTAB, 7: GMRES, 8: direct solver.

choices.3: conjugate gradient on a normal equation

keywords.help: Sets the accuracy needed for the computation of the diffusion of the velocities. Old default value = 1.E-5 until version V8P0.

keywords.keyword: MAXIMUM NUMBER OF ITERATIONS FOR DIFFUSION OF VELOCITIES
keywords.help: Limits the number of solver iterations for the diffusion of velocities.

Choice of preconditioning for the diffusion of velocities. Possible choices are: 0: no preconditioning, 2: diagonal, 3: diagonal with the condensed matrix, 5: diagonal with absolute values, 7: Crout, 11: Gauss-Seidel EBE, 13: matrix defined by the user, 14: diagonal and Crout, 17: direct solver on the vertical, 21: diagonal condensed and Crout, 34: diagonal and direct solver on the vertical.

choices.34: diagonal and direct solver on the vertical

keywords.keyword: OPTION OF SOLVER FOR DIFFUSION OF VELOCITIES
keywords.help: Dimension of Krylov space for the GMRES method (7). Old default value = 3 until version V8P0.
Sets the value of the implicitation coefficient for the diffusion step.

Choice of the solver for the Poisson Pressure Equation. Possible choices are: 1: conjugate gradient, 2: conjugate residual, 3: conjugate gradient on a normal equation, 4: minimum error, 5: squared conjugate gradient, 6: CGSTAB, 7: GMRES, 8: direct solver. Old default value = 1 (conjugate gradient) until version V8P0.

choices.3: conjugate gradient on a normal equation

keywords.help: Sets the precision needed for the computation of the Poisson Pressure Equation. Old default value = 1.E-4 until version V8P0.

keywords.keyword: MAXIMUM NUMBER OF ITERATIONS FOR PPE
keywords.help: Limits the number of solver iterations for the Poisson Pressure Equation.

Preconditioning for the Poisson Pressure Equation. Possible choices are: 0: no preconditioning, 2: diagonal, 3: diagonal with the condensed matrix, 5: diagonal with absolute values, 7: Crout, 11: Gauss-Seidel EBE, 13: matrix defined by the user, 14: diagonal and Crout, 17: direct solver on the vertical, 21: diagonal condensed and Crout, 34: diagonal and direct solver on the vertical.

choices.34: diagonal and direct solver on the vertical

keywords.help: Dimension of Krylov space for the GMRES method (7). Old default value = 3 until version V8P0.
Defines if an estimated pressure gradient is taken into account in the wave equation.
If YES, it enables to prescribe a velocity at the free surface coherent with the dynamic boundary condition.
Changes the free velocities on open boundaries to get a better divergence-free field.
Sets the value of the implicitation coefficient for water depth in the propagation step (cf. Principe note). The values lower than 0.5 give an instable scheme.
Sets the value of the implicitation coefficient for the velocity in the propagation step (cf. Principe note). The values lower than 0.5 give an instable scheme. Old default value = 1. until V8P0.
When NO, the specific treatments for tidal flats are by-passed. This spares time, but of course you must be sure that you have no tidal flats.

keywords.keyword: OPTION FOR THE TREATMENT OF TIDAL FLATS
keywords.help: Used if TIDAL FLATS is YES. Possible choices are: 1: equations solved everywhere with correction on tidal flats (corrected free surface gradient), 2: dry elements are frozen (tidal flats area are masked). Warning: mass-conservation may be altered. Only works in serial computation.

choices.1: EQUATIONS SOLVED EVERYWHERE WITH CORRECTION ON TIDAL FLATS

keywords.help: Only with OPTION FOR THE TREATMENT OF TIDAL FLATS = 1. Possible choices are: 0: no treatment, 1: smoothing, 2: flux control. If using option 2 with tidal flats, it is mandatory to set MASS-LUMPING FOR DEPTH = 1. Old default value = 1, i.e. smoothing, until V8P5.

keywords.keyword: TREATMENT ON TIDAL FLATS FOR VELOCITIES
keywords.help: Treatment of tidal flats at the diffusion step for velocities. 0: forced to zero, 1: value before masked.

keywords.keyword: THRESHOLD FOR VISCOSITY CORRECTION ON TIDAL FLATS
keywords.help: Below the threshold, viscosity will be progressively cancelled. See CLIP subroutine.
Sets the minimum water depth value H. Only used with OPTION FOR THE TREATMENT OF TIDAL FLATS = 2 i.e. dry elements are frozen (tidal flats area are masked) or with ELEMENTS MASKED BY USER = YES.
File name for the binary database 1 of tidal harmonic constants. In the case of the OSU satellite altimetry model (TPXO type), this file should be for free surface level, for instance h_tpxo7.2.
File name for the binary database 2 of tidal harmonic constants. In the case of the OSU satellite altimetry model (TPXO type), this file should be for tidal velocities, for instance u_tpxo7.2.

keywords.keyword: VELOCITIES IN BINARY DATABASE 2 FOR TIDE
keywords.help: Indicates if BINARY DATABASE 2 FOR TIDE contains velocities or circulations (h times velocities). For OSU solutions, let default value NO (circulation). For HAMTIDE, choose YES.

Geographic coordinates system in which the numerical model is built. Indicate the corresponding zone with the keyword. The possible choices are: 0: defined by the user, 1: WGS84 longitude/latitude in real degrees, 2: WGS84 Northern UTM, 3: WGS84 Southern UTM, 4: Lambert, 5: Mercator projection.

Number of zone when using a plane projection. Indicate the geographic system in which the numerical model is built with the keyword GEOGRAPHIC SYSTEM. Possible choices are: 1: Lambert 1 north, 2: Lambert 2 center, 3: Lambert 3 south, 4: Lambert 4 Corsica, 22: Lambert 22 extended, 93: Lambert 93, X: UTM zone with WGS84 (X is the number of the zone).
Name of file gr3df97a.txt, conversion grid for Lambert 93.
Coefficient to calibrate the sea level. This coefficient usually corresponds to the mean sea level or a close value.

keywords.keyword: GLOBAL NUMBER OF THE POINT TO CALIBRATE HIGH WATER
keywords.help: Global number of the point (between 1 and the number of boundary nodes in the 2D mesh) with respect to which the tidal constituents have their phase shifted to start the calculation with a high water (for schematic tides only). This point has to be a maritime boundary node. Only harmonic constants databases like TPXO are concerned.
For tidal solutions developed by OSU (e.g. TPXO) only. Inference of minor constituents from the ones read in input files linked to keywords BINARY DATABASE 1 FOR TIDE and BINARY DATABASE 2 FOR TIDE.

Initial velocity components computed from a tidal solution from OSU (e.g. TPXO) or HAMTIDE. NO to prevent from an initialisation with too big tidal velocities. For tidal solutions coming from OSU (e.g. TPXO) or HAMTIDE only.

keywords.keyword: MINIMUM DEPTH TO COMPUTE TIDAL VELOCITIES INITIAL CONDITIONS
keywords.help: Minimum value of water depth above which initial conditions for tidal velocities are computed. Otherwise, the velocity components are equal to 0. For tidal solutions coming from OSU only (e.g. TPXO).
Take in account atmospheric pressure at tidal boundary conditions. Inverted barometer method used to compute the shift.
The tide generating force is taken into account.

Option for tidal boundary conditions. For real tides, option 1 is recommended. This keyword has been an array with a value given per liquid boundary, separated by semicolons, since version 7.1. This enables to have tidal conditions (or not) computed on liquid boundaries with prescribed velocities or depths, avoiding a clash when using weirs in the domain. 0 codes for conditions other than tidal. BEWARE since version 7.1! Old models must be changed if their tidal boundary is not number 1. In that case this keyword must be changed and more values given. Possible calibration with the keywords COEFFICIENT TO CALIBRATE TIDAL RANGE, COEFFICIENT TO CALIBRATE TIDAL VELOCITIES, and COEFFICIENT TO CALIBRATE SEA LEVEL. Possible choices are: 0: No tide, 1: Real tide (recommended methodology), 2: Astronomical tide, 3: Mean spring tide, 4: Mean tide, 5: Mean neap tide, 6: Astronomical neap tide, 7: Real tide (methodology before 2010).

Gives the name of the data base used to automatically generate the boundary conditions. Possible choices are: 1: JMJ, 2: TPXO, 3: MISCELLANEOUS (LEGOS-NEA, FES20XX, PREVIMER...). For JMJ, indicate the location of the files bdd_jmj and geofin with keywords ASCII DATABASE FOR TIDE and TIDAL MODEL FILE. For TPXO, LEGOS-NEA, FES20XX and PREVIMER, the user has to download files of harmonic constituents on the internet.
Name of the file containing the harmonic constants extracted from the tidal model file (JMJ) or other atlases (FES, NEA, PREVIMER).
Geometry file of the model from which harmonic constituents are extracted (JMJ only).

Format of the TIDAL MODEL FILE. Possible choices are: SERAFIN : classical single precision format in TELEMAC, SERAFIND: classical double precision format in TELEMAC, MED : MED double precision format based on HDF5.
File name for the tide data base of harmonic constituents extracted from the TIDAL MODEL FILE.
Coefficient to calibrate the tidal range of tidal wave at tidal open boundary conditions.
Coefficient to calibrate the tidal velocities of tidal wave at tidal open boundary conditions. Default value 999999. means that the square root of COEFFICIENT TO CALIBRATE TIDAL RANGE is taken.

keywords.keyword: LOCAL NUMBER OF THE POINT TO CALIBRATE HIGH WATER
keywords.help: Local number between 1 and the number of tidal boundary points (of the HARMONIC CONSTANTS FILE) where the tidal boundary conditions are computed with JMJ, NEA, FES, PREVIMER databases (except TPXO-type databases). The tidal constituents have their phase shifted with respect to this point to start the simulation with a high water (for schematic tides only).

keywords.keyword: MINIMUM DEPTH TO COMPUTE TIDAL VELOCITIES BOUNDARY CONDITIONS
keywords.help: Minimum value of water depth used to compute tidal boundary conditions for velocities if the water depths are too small. For tidal solutions coming from OSU only (e.g. TPXO).

Maximum number of drogues in the computation. The user must then fill the subroutine USER_FLOT3D specifying the coordinates of the starting points, their departure and arrival times. The trajectory of drogues is recorded in the ASCII DROGUES FILE or the BINARY DROGUES FILE that must be given in the steering file.
ASCII results file with positions of drogues.
Binary results file with positions of drogues.
Format of the BINARY DROGUES FILE. Possible choices are: BKBINPCL: binary PCL format native to Blue Kenue, TECPLOT: original TecPlot format (ASCII).
Number of time steps between 2 outputs of drogues positions in the binary file. It does not disturb the quality of the computation of the trajectory.
Contains data for the oil spill model. If present in the steering file, triggers the oil spill model since release 9.0 without boolean keyword OIL SPILL MODEL.
For particles: drogues, oil spills. If no turbulence is activated, this stochastic diffusion is not considered during the particle transport.
Number of culverts, tubes or bridges treated as source terms. They must be described as sources in the domain and their features are given in the CULVERTS DATA FILE (see written documentation).
Description of culverts/bridges existing in the model.
Option for the treatment of culverts. There are two options in TELEMAC-3D based on Bodhaine (1968) and Carlier (1976) formulae. Read the TELEMAC-3D theory guide for more informations.

Specifies the horizontal turbulence model. The available choices are: 1: constant viscosity, 3: k-epsilon model, 4: Smagorinski, 5: Spalart-Allmaras, 7: k-omega model, 9: DES model (Detached Eddy Simulation). Caution: if option 1 is chosen, give the right COEFFICIENT FOR... DIFFUSION OF VELOCITIES... If option 3 ou 7 is chosen, this parameter must get its real physical value of molecular diffusivity, generally about 10^-6 because it is used as well in the turbulence model.

Specifies the vertical turbulence model. The available choices are: 1: constant viscosity, 2: mixing length, 3: k-epsilon model, 4: Smagorinski, 5: Spalart-Allmaras, 6: GOTM, 7: k-omega model, 9: DES model (Detached Eddy Simulation). Caution: if option 1 is chosen, give the right COEFFICIENT FOR... DIFFUSION OF VELOCITIES... If option 3 ou 7 is chosen, this parameter must get its real physical value of molecular diffusivity, generally about 10^-6 because it is used as well in the turbulence model. Old default value = 1 (constant viscosity) until release 8.5.

keywords.keyword: COEFFICIENT FOR HORIZONTAL DIFFUSION OF VELOCITIES
keywords.help: Sets, in an even way for the whole domain, the value of the coefficient of global (dynamic+turbulent) viscosity for the horizontal direction. This value may have a significant effect both on the shapes and sizes of recirculation zones.

keywords.keyword: COEFFICIENT FOR VERTICAL DIFFUSION OF VELOCITIES
keywords.help: Sets, in an even way for the whole domain, the value of the coefficient of global (dynamic+turbulent) viscosity for the horizontal direction. This value may have a significant effect both on the shapes and sizes of recirculation zones.

Specifies the mixing length model used for vertical turbulence. Possible choices are: 1: Prandtl (suits such flows with a strong barotropic component as tidal flows), 3: Nezu and Nakagawa, 5: Quetin (better representation of wind drift), 6: Tsanis (better representation of wind drift). 4 (jet) has been suppressed. Old default value = 1 (Prandtl) until release 8.5.
Specifies the type of damping function used (when using mixing length turbulence model). The possible choices are: 0: nothing, 1: user programmed (in USER_DRIUTI), 2: Viollet, 3: Munk and Anderson.
Ratio between eddy viscosity and eddy diffusivity.
Value of Von Karman constant.
File containing parameters of GOTM. Use in combination with VERTICAL TURBULENCE MODEL = 6.
Ratio between the fictitious bed and the grid size above the bed.

keywords.keyword: OPTION FOR THE BOUNDARY CONDITIONS OF K-EPSILON
keywords.help: Computation of the lateral boundary conditions of k and epsilon. Possible choices are: 1: no turbulence = the minimum values KMIN and EMIN defined in CSTKEP, 2: Hans Burchard formula.

Way of computing the velocity derivatives along z only for a mixing length model over the vertical: 1: linear derivative (classic), 2: logarithmic derivative (better for logarithmic profiles) between the bottom and 0.2 times the water depth. Option 2 allows getting better results when modelling the velocity profile near the bottom.

Sets the advection scheme for the k-epsilon model or Spalart-Allmaras model. Possible choices are: 0: no convection, 1: characteristics, 2: SUPG, 3: Leo Postma scheme, 4: MURD scheme N, SCHEME OPTION FOR ADVECTION OF VELOCITIES/TRACERS/K-EPSILON): 1: classical explicit scheme; 2: 1st order predictor-corrector; 3: 2nd order predictor-corrector; 4: implicit scheme compatible with tidal flats; NUMBER OF CORRECTIONS OF DISTRIBUTIVE SCHEMES: sets the number of sub-iterations for the 1st and 2nd order predictor-corrector schemes (a value around 4 is recommended). 5: MURD scheme PSI, SCHEME OPTION FOR ADVECTION OF VELOCITIES/TRACERS/K-EPSILON): 1: classical explicit scheme; 2: 1st order predictor-corrector; 3: 2nd order predictor-corrector; 4: implicit scheme compatible with tidal flats; NUMBER OF CORRECTIONS OF DISTRIBUTIVE SCHEMES: sets the number of sub-iterations for the 1st and 2nd order predictor-corrector schemes (a value around 4 is recommended). 13: Leo Postma for tidal flats, 14: explicit N-scheme for tidal flats. Default values for SCHEME FOR ADVECTION OF K-EPSILON = 5 + SCHEME OPTION FOR ADVECTION OF K-EPSILON = 4 give LIPS scheme. Old default value = 1 (characteristics) until version V8P0.

keywords.keyword: SCHEME OPTION FOR ADVECTION OF K-EPSILON
keywords.help: If present replaces and has priority over: OPTION FOR CHARACTERISTICS and SUPG OPTION. If N or PSI scheme: 1: explicit, 2: predictor-corrector, 3: predictor-corrector second-order in time, 4: implicit (compatible with tidal flats). If no tidal flats, option 2 is faster. Old default value = 1 (explicit) until version V8P0.
Monitors the choice of the diffusion scheme for k and epsilon. Possible choices are: 0: no diffusion, 1: implicit.

Choice of the solver for the diffusion of k and epsilon. but also nu. Possible choices are: 1: conjugate gradient, 2: conjugate residual, 3: conjugate gradient on a normal equation, 4: minimum error, 5: squared conjugate gradient, 6: CGSTAB, 7: GMRES, 8: direct solver.

choices.3: conjugate gradient on a normal equation

keywords.help: Sets the accuracy needed for the computation of the diffusion of the k-epsilon or Spalart-Allmaras models. Old default value = 1.E-6 until version V8P0.

keywords.keyword: MAXIMUM NUMBER OF ITERATIONS FOR DIFFUSION OF K-EPSILON
keywords.help: Limits the number of solver iterations for the diffusion of k-epsilon or nu.

Choice of preconditioning for the diffusion of the k-epsilon model or Spalart-Allmaras model. Possible choices are: 0: no preconditioning, 2: diagonal, 3: diagonal with the condensed matrix, 5: diagonal with absolute values, 7: Crout, 11: Gauss-Seidel EBE, 13: matrix defined by the user, 14: diagonal and Crout, 17: direct solver on the vertical, 21: diagonal condensed and Crout, 34: diagonal and direct solver on the vertical.

choices.34: diagonal and direct solver on the vertical

keywords.keyword: OPTION OF SOLVER FOR DIFFUSION OF K-EPSILON
keywords.help: Dimension of Krylov space for the GMRES method (7). Old default value = 3 until version V8P0.

keywords.keyword: TREATMENT ON TIDAL FLATS FOR K-EPSILON
keywords.help: Treatment of tidal flats at the diffusion step for k and epsilon. 0: forced to zero, 1: value before masked.
Defines the number of tracers.
Name of tracers in 32 characters, 16 for the name, 16 for the unit.

keywords.keyword: VALUES OF TRACERS IN THE RAIN
keywords.help: Sets the value of the tracers in the rain.

keywords.keyword: VALUE OF THE TRACERS AT THE SOURCES
keywords.help: Sets the value of the tracers at the sources. All tracers for the first source, then all tracers for the second source, etc. (see user manual). For example, if there are 3 tracers (T1, T2 and T3) and 2 sources (S1 and S2), the following syntax is used: S1_T1;S1_T2;S1_T3;S2_T1;S2_T2;S2_T3 10.0; 10.0; 0.0; 0.0; 10.0; 10.0

Gives the type of the law of density used in the case of active tracers. The sediment is considered active with its own law by default. The possible choices are: 0: no variation of density with tracers such as temperature or salinity, but variation of density with sediment if present, 1: function of the temperature (and sediment if present), 2: function of the salinity (and sediment if present), 3: function of the temperature and salinity (and sediment if present), 4: user-defined BETA coefficients (and effect of the sediment with its own behaviour if present), 5: no variation of density. No tracer is considered to compute density (in particular temperature, salinity or sediment). Density is then constant, equal to the value given by AVERAGE WATER DENSITY (default = 1,025~kg/m^3). The sediment and other tracers are forced to be passive, 6: Jackett et al. 2006.
Reference value of tracers corresponding to the given density when using DENSITY LAW = 4 (one value per tracer).
Unit: K^-1. This coefficient is used to define the evolution of the water density with respect to the tracer concentration when using DENSITY LAW = 4 (one value per tracer).
Determines the imposed value of tracers at the first boundary, then at the second, and so on, with the same logic as VALUE OF THE TRACERS AT THE SOURCES.

Specifies the type of profiles of tracer concentration on the vertical. There are as many values to be given as the product of the number of tracers and the number of open boundaries. Possible choices are: 0: user defined (with tracers values), 1: constant, 2: Rouse equilibrium, constant (diluted tracer) or Rouse (sediment), 3: Rouse (normalized) and imposed concentration, 4: Rouse modified with molecular viscosity, 5: user defined (normalized) and imposed concentration.

choices.4: 'Modified Rouse profile accounting for molecular viscosity
choices.5: 'Normalized user defined profile and imposed concentration

keywords.help: Sets the initial values of tracer(s). Required value(s) separated with a semicolumn ; if more than one. The number of supplied values must be equal to the number of declared tracers.

Sets the advection scheme for the tracers (one integer per tracer). Possible choices are: 0: no convection, 1: characteristics, 2: explicit + SUPG, 3: explicit Leo Postma, 4: explicit + MURD scheme N, 5: explicit + MURD scheme PSI, 13: Leo Postma for tidal flats, 14: N-scheme for tidal flats. Default values for SCHEME FOR ADVECTION OF TRACERS = 5 + SCHEME OPTION FOR ADVECTION OF TRACERS = 4 give LIPS scheme.

keywords.keyword: SCHEME OPTION FOR ADVECTION OF TRACERS
keywords.help: If present replaces and has priority over: OPTION FOR CHARACTERISTICS and SUPG OPTION. If N or PSI scheme: 1: explicit, 2: predictor-corrector, 3: predictor-corrector second-order in time, 4: implicit (compatible with tidal flats). Default value = 4. If no tidal flats, option 2 is faster. It is possible to have different values per tracer. Old default value = 1 (explicit) until version V8P0.
Monitors the choice of the diffusion scheme for tracers. Possible choices are: 0: no diffusion, 1: implicit.

Choice of the solver for the diffusion of tracers (one integer per tracer). Possible choices are: 1: conjugate gradient, 2: conjugate residual, 3: conjugate gradient on a normal equation, 4: minimum error, 5: squared conjugate gradient, 6: CGSTAB, 7: GMRES, 8: direct solver.

choices.3: conjugate gradient on a normal equation

keywords.help: Sets the accuracy needed for the computation of the diffusion of the tracers. It is possible to have different values per tracer since release V8P4. Default value = 1.E-8. Old default value = 1.E-6 until version V7P3.

keywords.keyword: MAXIMUM NUMBER OF ITERATIONS FOR DIFFUSION OF TRACERS
keywords.help: Limits the number of solver iterations for the diffusion of tracer(s). It is possible to have different values per tracer since release V8P4. Default value = 60.

Choice of preconditioning for the diffusion of tracers (one integer per tracer). Possible choices are: 0: no preconditioning, 2: diagonal, 3: diagonal with the condensed matrix, 5: diagonal with absolute values, 7: Crout, 11: Gauss-Seidel EBE, 13: matrix defined by the user, 14: diagonal and Crout, 17: direct solver on the vertical, 21: diagonal condensed and Crout, 34: diagonal and direct solver on the vertical.

choices.34: diagonal and direct solver on the vertical

keywords.keyword: OPTION OF SOLVER FOR DIFFUSION OF TRACERS
keywords.help: Dimension of Krylov space for the GMRES method (7). It is possible to have different integers per tracer since release V8P4. Default value = 5. Old default value = 3 until version V8P0.

keywords.keyword: TREATMENT ON TIDAL FLATS FOR TRACERS
keywords.help: Treatment of tidal flats at the diffusion step for tracers. 0: forced to zero, 1: value before masked. Use choice 1 to ensure conservation of tracer(s).

keywords.keyword: COEFFICIENT FOR HORIZONTAL DIFFUSION OF TRACERS
keywords.help: Sets the values of the horizontal diffusion of tracers. These values may have a significant effect on the evolution of tracers in time. Since version 7.1, it has been an array, with one value per tracer, separated by semicolons.

keywords.keyword: COEFFICIENT FOR VERTICAL DIFFUSION OF TRACERS
keywords.help: Sets the values of the vertical diffusion of tracers. These values may have a significant effect on the evolution of tracers in time. Since version 7.1, it has been an array, with one value per tracer, separated by semicolons.
If YES, sediment transport is modelled.
Value of the sediment density (kg/m^3).

Time step for the modelling consolidation, which can be greater than the hydrodynamic time step. This parameter is used if CONSOLIDATION MODEL = 1 (Empirical multilayer model) or 2 (Gibson model (Lenormant)).
Tells if the sediment is cohesive or not.
Used to determine the critical bed shear stress value.
If YES, calculation of mixed sediment transport, there will be one cohesive sediment and one non cohesive sediment.
Number of cohesive sediment bed layers, should be less than 20.

keywords.keyword: READ CRITICAL BED SHEAR STRESS PER LAYER
keywords.help: Decides if erosion shear stress at each layer is read from GEOMETRY FILE.

Name of the file into which the sedimentological computation results (thickness and concentration of the mud bed...) shall be written, the periodicity being given by the keyword GRAPHIC PRINTOUT PERIOD.

Binary file type used for writing the results file. This type depends on the machine on which the file was generated. The possible values are as follows: IBM, for a file on an IBM (from a CRAY), I3E, for a file on an HP (from a CRAY), STD, binary type of the machine on which the user is working. In that case, normal READ and WRITE commands are used.

Name of a file containing the sedimentological parameters (thickness and concentration of the bed...), results of an earlier computation which was made on the same mesh. The last recorded time step will provide the initial conditions for the new computation.
Sets the value of the diameter D50 for non cohesive sediments.

keywords.keyword: RATIO BETWEEN SKIN FRICTION AND MEAN DIAMETER
keywords.help: Ratio for the computation of skin friction. skin roughness = ratio x mean diameter.

Formula to predict the skin bed roughness: 0: No correction (TAUP = TOB) see also RATIO ENTRE LA RUGOSITE DE PEAU ET LE DIAMETRE MOYEN S3D_KSPRATIO, 1: Flat bed (KSP = S3D_KSPRATIO x S3D_D50), 2: Ripple correction factor (not yet implemented).

keywords.keyword: INITIAL PERCENTAGE OF NON COHESIVE SEDIMENT
keywords.help: Initial percentage of non cohesive sediment (mixed sediments).
Dry density of the mud-bed layers in g/L starting form the bottom upwards.

keywords.keyword: CRITICAL EROSION SHEAR STRESS OF THE MUD LAYERS
keywords.help: Critical erosion shear stress of the mud per layer (N/m^2). Needs to be defined for each layer (N/m^2), starting from the condolidated bottom layer upwards.
Sediment layers thickness (m) for initialisation.

keywords.keyword: SOLVER FOR DIFFUSION OF THE SEDIMENT
keywords.help: Choice of the solver for the sediment equation. Possible choices are: 1: conjugate gradient, 2: conjugate residual, 3: conjugate gradient on a normal equation, 4: minimum error, 5: squared conjugate gradient, 6: CGSTAB, 7: GMRES, 8: direct solver.

choices.3: conjugate gradient on a normal equation

keywords.help: Sets the accuracy needed for the computation of the diffusion of sediments. Old default value = 1.E-6 until version V8P0.

keywords.keyword: MAXIMUM NUMBER OF ITERATIONS FOR DIFFUSION OF SEDIMENT
keywords.help: Limits the number of solver iterations for the diffusion of sediment.

keywords.keyword: PRECONDITIONING FOR DIFFUSION OF THE SEDIMENT
keywords.help: Choice of the preconditioning in the sediment diffusion system that the convergence is speeded up when it is being solved. Possible choices are: 0: no preconditioning, 2: diagonal, 3: diagonal with the condensed matrix, 5: diagonal with absolute values, 7: Crout, 11: Gauss-Seidel EBE, 13: matrix defined by the user, 14: diagonal and Crout, 17: direct solver on the vertical, 21: diagonal condensed and Crout, 34: diagonal and direct solver on the vertical. Some operations (either 2 or 3 diagonal preconditioning) can be performed concurrently with the others. Only prime numbers are therefore kept to denote the preconditioning operations. When several of them are to be performed concurrently, the product of relevant options shall be done.

choices.34: diagonal and direct solver on the vertical

keywords.keyword: OPTION OF SOLVER FOR DIFFUSION OF THE SEDIMENT
keywords.help: Dimension of Krylov space for the GMRES method (7). Old default value = 3 until version V8P0.

keywords.keyword: THRESHOLD FOR SEDIMENT FLUX CORRECTION ON TIDAL FLATS
keywords.help: Below this limiting depth, all sediment erosion rates are set to zero. See subroutine FLUSED.
Value of the critical bottom shear stress under which deposition of cohesive sediments occurs.
The bed volume concentration S3D_CFDEP = (1-S3D_XKV) x S3D_RHOS is used to calculate the bed evolution of non-cohesive sand transport.
Value of the erosion coefficient used in Partheniades formula in kg/m^2/s.
Constant sediment settling velocity in m/s (>0 since v6.3). Prescribed value if INFLUENCE OF TURBULENCE ON SETTLING VELOCITY = NO.
Non cohesive sediment settling velocity.
Choice of the vertical scheme for diffusion and settling of sediment: 0: Implicit-diffusion scheme, 1: Implicit-convection scheme (Tridiagonal matrix solver), 2: set_fall.f
Decides if hindered formulation is to be used to compute settling velocity for mud.
The sediment concentration at which sediment forms a weak soil in kg/m^3. These values are needed when HINDERED SETTLING = YES.
The sediment concentration at which hindered settling is initiated. These values are needed when HINDERED SETTLING = YES.
Type of hindered settling: 1: Whitehouse et al. (2000) - working, 2: Winterwerp (1999) - not currently working.
1: Zyserman and Fredsoe, equilibrium formula, 3: Van Rijn formula (1987).
Decides if hindered formulation is to be used to compute settling velocity for mud.
Type of flocculation formula: 1: Van Leussen, 2: Soulsby et al. (2013).

When the influence of turbulence on the settling velocity is modelled, this coefficient traduces the formation of flocs by turbulence (coefficient a of Van Leussen formula). Value to be imposed if INFLUENCE OF TURBULENCE ON SETTLING VELOCITY = YES.

When the influence of turbulence on the settling velocity is modelled, this coefficient traduces the breaking of flocs by turbulence (coefficient b of Van Leussen formula). Value to be imposed if INFLUENCE OF TURBULENCE ON SETTLING VELOCITY = YES.

Reference thickness considered for the creation of new bed layers. This parameter is used if CONSOLIDATION MODEL = 2 (Gibson model (Lenormant)). With this model, the sediment which settles on the bottom arrives at first in the fresh deposit layer. When the thickness of this layer is equal to the BED LAYERS THICKNESS, a new mud layer is added to the mud bed.

keywords.keyword: MAXIMUM CONCENTRATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED MUD
keywords.help: Maximum concentration which may be reached by a mud layer during consolidation. This value is used if CONSOLIDATION MODEL = 2 (Gibson model (Lenormant)).

Array which contains the residence times of the mud bed layers (the first value is related to the bottom layer and the last one to the top layer). These values are needed when CONSOLIDATION MODEL = 1 (Empirical multilayer model).

If this key word is equal to YES, consolidation is simulated thanks to a multi-layers model: the bed layers are characterized by their residence time which is the time after which the quantity of mud which remains in a layer goes into a more consolidated layer.
Choice of the consolidation model: 1: Empirical multilayer model, 2: Gibson model (Lenormant).

List of codes to be coupled with TELEMAC-3D: TOMAWAC: internal coupling with TOMAWAC, forces are constant along the depth, TOMAWACT3D: internal coupling with TOMAWAC, forces are 3D, TOMAWAC2: internal coupling with TOMAWAC, forces are constant along the depth, meshes and domains can be different, TOMAWACT3D2: internal coupling with TOMAWAC, forces are 3D, meshes and domains can be different, WAQTEL: internal coupling with WAQTEL, DELWAQ: will yield results file for DELWAQ, GAIA: internal coupling with GAIA, KHIONE: internal coupling with KHIONE.
TOMAWAC parameter file in case of internal coupling.
Sets the coupling period with the TOMAWAC module, in number of time steps. By default, it is coupled at every time step.
Allows to take into account the momentum lost by waves due to bottom friction. You need a fine mesh around the bottom to be precise.

Gives the water quality process number, defined as a multiplicative combination of prime numbers (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19) with 0 and 1 having a special role: 0: all, 1: none, 2: O2, 3: BIOMASS, 5: EUTRO, 7: MICROPOL, 11: THERMIC, 13: AED2, 17: Degradation law, 19: Ghost process for ice modelling. Example: 110 = 2x5x11 activates O2, EUTRO and THERMIC together. It is noted that AED2 should be used on its own, for the time being, without possible combination with other processes.
File for physical parameters of water quality processes (local ones of TELEMAC-3D-WAQTEL not those of DELWAQ).

Defines the number of user derivatives, within the framework of the algorithmic differentiation.
Name of user derivatives in 32 characters, 16 for the name, 16 for the unit.

Enables the symbolic linear solver for AD.

Iterative linear solvers: derivative convergence test for AD.
Partitioning tool selection: 1: METIS, 2: SCOTCH, 3: PARMETIS, 4: PTSCOTCH.
